public_headline: FBI Interview Records Witness Account of Unexplained Light in 2023
public_tldr: This is page 2 of a two-page FBI witness interview form (FD-302) documenting a UAP sighting in September 2023. The witness initially thought the light was a meteor burning up in the atmosphere, but the document is so heavily redacted that most details — including the witness's name, exact date, and location — are obscured.
public_narrative:
This document is an FBI FD-302 form, the standard template the Bureau uses to summarize witness interviews. It records a US citizen's first-hand account of encountering an unidentified anomalous phenomenon (UAP) at a US test site in September 2023. The specific day within that month is redacted.

Only page 2 of 2 is available in this release. That means most of the substantive detail from the interview — what the witness saw, how long it lasted, any physical evidence — is missing entirely. What survives on this page is a single descriptive detail: the witness initially believed the light they observed was a meteor coming straight toward them and burning up in the atmosphere.

The document is extremely redacted throughout. The witness's name, the precise date, and the specific location are all blacked out. No agency conclusion or follow-up assessment is visible in the available page. There is no indication in the surviving text of what the FBI ultimately determined the object to be, or whether any further investigation was conducted.

Because this is a single witness's subjective recollection as summarized by an FBI interviewer, and the majority of the interview content is either on the missing first page or hidden under redactions, the document on its own provides very limited information about the incident.
public_caveats: Only page 2 of a 2-page document is available — most substantive details from the interview are on the missing first page.
The document is extremely redacted: the witness's identity, exact date, and specific location are all obscured.
This is a single-source account — one witness's subjective recollection, summarized by an FBI interviewer, with no corroborating evidence visible.
The witness's own first interpretation was that the light was a meteor, which indicates uncertainty about what was actually observed.
No agency conclusion or assessment is visible in the available material — there is no indication of what the FBI determined the object to be.
